arguments.text: 6000 m, legs 1250 m out-and-back (4.8 legs). Goal: even effort near pod sustainable shaft power (~175 W; pod CP 169 W, reserve 16 kJ, test may be 10-25 pct off). Let the hard start settle by ~3 min; if shaft power still well above ~180 W after that, ease. Mid-race (around 2000-3500 m) consider a short piece to test whether CP is higher or lower (HR trend at a fixed effort). Watch for incidents: speed loss at steady pod power (weed, drag), pod vs GPS mismatch (pod drift), radio messages (course changes). Finish sprint from about 400-600 m to go depending on reserve.

arguments.message: GPS speed well below what pod power should give: weed, drag or pod reading high?

arguments.text: 3.2 min: start settled at ~130 s. Pod fell 244->185 W and rate 73->67, but boat-model power only 131->123 and water speed 3.20->3.14; hull fit could not fit one share for both (share 0.54 vs 0.66). Either pod reads low since ~130 s or lower rate is more efficient. HR 170, trend +1 bpm/min at 150-195 s. Paddler says 5/10, plenty. Pod reserve 37 pct. Test: watch HR trend at steady ~185 W pod 190-330 s; levels off -> CP likely higher than 169; keeps climbing -> CP right, ease.

Next: if HR keeps creeping < 1.5 bpm/min while pod reserve runs toward 0 without a fade, CP is underestimated -> raise critical_power_pod_w. If HR climbs faster or speed fades, ease.

Read as: effort above true CP, paddler overrates self. Cued ease at 441 s. Experiment: after the ease settles (~500-620 s), measure HR trend at the new effort. Level/falling -> CP between new effort and 187; still climbing -> CP below new effort, ease more.

arguments.text: 6000 m, legs 1250 m out-and-back; current ~0.25 m/s helps on out legs (odd legs), hurts on back legs (even). CP pod now believed ~183 W (176-192; test said 169, too low), pod reserve ~46 pct at 715 s. Rudder fouling cleared at 645 s. Plan: hold ~CP (183-187 W pod) on leg 3 (out, 2500-3750 m); on leg 4 (back, into current, from 3750 m = 2250 to go) ask a +4 to +5 pct piece for about 300 s (more power where the boat is slow); finish: from ~700 m to go start the sprint if reserve allows (pod reserve > 30 pct), else 400-500 m. Watch: drag step (push_local - push_along below -0.07: back-stroke), forced pod drop (reserve empty: then CP lower, ease), HR climbing > 1 bpm/min at steady effort (CP lower).

HR slope model suggests CP ~180 (0.86 bpm/min at 189 W early, 0.30 at 183 W). Pod reserve at 183 W CP: 46 pct. Speed_loss watch tightened to -0.08 (old -0.25 missed the 0.09 m/s step).

arguments.name: critical_power_pod_w
arguments.evidence: Forced drop at ~750 s: pod 185 -> 133 W at same rate, HR fell 176 -> 162, paddler 9/10 (says just a breather). Reserve ran out. Energy balance with 16 kJ reserve: 244 W x 125 s start + ~185 W x 630 s empties it at CP ~173-174. HR plateau at 176 was misleading (not proof of being below CP).

arguments.text: 6000 m, legs 1250 m out-and-back; current ~0.256 m/s helps out legs (3, 5), hurts back legs (4). Share of pod power reaching boat ~0.62. TRUE CP pod ~174 W (169-179): paddler blew up at ~750 s after holding ~185 W (my raise to 183 was wrong). Paddler overrates self: do not trust feel, cap effort. Plan: let forced recovery run; once pod power is back near 165+, cue hold with a ground-pace target per leg: out legs ~154 s/500 (about 169 W), back leg 4 ~180 s/500 (about 179 W); re-cue at each turn since the target is over ground. Finish: sprint from ~400-500 m to go using what reserve has refilled (pod reserve shown at CP 174). Watches: drag step (back-stroke), forced drop.

13.1 min: BLOW-UP at ~750 s, pod 185 -> 133 W at rate 67, HR 176 -> 162, paddler 9/10 calls it a breather. Reset CP pod to 174 (169-179), boat 112; pod reserve 12 pct at 790 s and refilling. Lesson: HR plateau at 176 did not mean below CP. Pace targets (ground) computed from fit: out leg 3.26 m/s at 174 W = 153 s/500; back 2.75 m/s = 182 s/500.
